ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all directors, officers, shareholders with at least 10% interest, and ultimate beneficial owners against: (i) Canadian sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Masha's Law); (ii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, given USD-denominated payment rails; (iii) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) FINTRAC guidance on domestic and foreign politically exposed persons; (v) adverse media and regulatory enforcement databases. Enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs, sanctioned jurisdictions, or opaque ownership chains; standard CDD applies to the Low_Risk_Standard tier for ISIC 6202 computer programming services.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.mlro_institution_registration_if_applica: Not applicable: the entity is not itself an MSB, trust company, or financial intermediary requiring FINTRAC registration under the PCMLTFA, provided the ODC holds no client funds and does not transact in virtual currency.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES), Government of Alberta, filed through Authorized Service Providers; official program portal: https://www.albertacorporateregistry.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in English or French, or a combination thereof; a pre-clearance NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report is mandatory; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin characters without altering phonetics; the legal designator must be 'Limited', 'Incorporated', 'Corporation', or the abbreviations 'Ltd.', 'Inc.', 'Corp.', and the name must not be confusingly similar to an existing registered or reserved name or a protected trademark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon NUANS-based rejection, the applicant may: (i) resubmit a revised distinguishing name within the same 90-day search window, supported by a new or updated NUANS report; (ii) request an informal administrative review with the Alberta Corporate Registry name desk of Service Alberta; (iii) if the rejection is arbitrary or erroneous, apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSA 2000, c J-5; and (iv) if a third party asserts a confusingly similar name or trademark, the objection is adjudicated under ABCA s. 22, and the Registry may order a name change.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted. ABCA requires a real street address in Alberta at which legal process may be served; a mail-forwarding-only virtual office satisfies the Registry for incorporation but may fail bank account-opening customer due diligence and Canada Revenue Agency substance checks. For an ISIC 6202 Offshore_Dev_Center, a full-service virtual office with physical reception and in-person document acceptance is market-acceptable, but a physical Alberta workplace with resident personnel is recommended to support a permanent-establissement defense and transfer-pricing documentation under Income Tax Act s. 247.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Negligible from the corporate registry (estimated below 1% unannounced inspection probability); moderate from the Canada Revenue Agency for a non-resident-controlled ODC (estimated 10–15% probability of an audit or field visit within the first three years), driven primarily by transfer-pricing and permanent-establishment verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 — ss. 6-10 (incorporation and articles), s. 11 (certificate of incorporation), s. 101 (registered office), s. 105 (by-law making power), s. 106 (first directors), s. 121 (officers), s. 114.2 (annual return)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Corporate Registry Services, Service Alberta (online portal and accredited service providers)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 — Articles of Incorporation under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow or pre-funded deposit required; articles may authorize one or more classes of shares (e.g., Unlimited Class A common shares at CAD 0.01 par value); consideration may be money, property, or past services as determined by the board
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: 1. RESOLVED that the subscriber share subscription stated in the Articles of Incorporation is ratified, and 100 common shares are issued at CAD 0.01 per share upon payment; 2. RESOLVED that the registered office is established at the postal address listed in Form 1, Alberta, which also serves as the corporate records office; 3. RESOLVED that the following officers are appointed: President and Chief Executive Officer, Corporate Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer, each serving until resignation or removal by the Board; 4. RESOLVED that the President and CEO and the Secretary are jointly authorized to lodge all filings with the Alberta Corporate Registry and the Canada Revenue Agency and to bind the Corporation generally.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Clearance (or Numbered-Name Election)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Corporate Registry Services, Service Alberta via accredited NUANS search providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS search for the proposed distinctive English corporate name and obtain a Name Search Report; verify the corporate designator (Ltd., Corp., Inc.); the name is reserved for 90 days; alternatively, adopt a numbered name in the format '1234567 Alberta Ltd.' generated from the registry system, which requires no NUANS search.
required_dossiers: NUANS Name Search Report (if using a distinctive name)
Proposed corporate name memorandum
Incorporator identification particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for distinctiveness, file a new NUANS search or convert to a numbered-name incorporation; name search fees are non-refundable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Corporate Registry Services, Service Alberta (online filing via the corporate registry application or authorized service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and execute Form 1 — Articles of Incorporation under ss. 6-10 ABCA: set out share structure (e.g., unlimited Class A voting common shares), restrictions on share transfers, physical registered office address in Alberta, and first directors' full names and residential addresses; submit with the CAD 275 filing fee; receive the electronically sealed Certificate of Incorporation and an incorporation abstract.
required_dossiers: Form 1 — Articles of Incorporation (executed)
NUANS name report or numbered-name declaration
First directors' consents and residential addresses
Physical registered office address (not a P.O. Box)
Payment of statutory filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a notice of defect, correct the cited deficiency in name, share classes, or director information and re-file within the statutory cure window (generally 30 days); no duplicate fee is assessed for registry-initiated corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of By-Laws, Organizational Resolutions, and Initial Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary (internal governance; minute book records; no registry filing other than subsequent Form 6 director changes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting under s. 105 ABCA; adopt By-law No. 1 (general operating by-law); approve officer appointments, banking resolutions, and authorized signatories; issue the initial common share certificates to the subscriber upon receipt of par-value consideration; create the corporate register, minute book, and securities register; file any later director changes on Form 6 within 15 days under s. 113 ABCA.
required_dossiers: By-law No. 1 draft
Organizational board resolution
Share certificates and securities register
Director and officer consent declarations
Minute book and corporate seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Not applicable for registry purposes; procedural defects are cured by an amending board or shareholder resolution entered in the minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of CRA Business Number and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO) portal; Alberta corporate income tax is administered federally under a collection agreement, so no separate Alberta corporate tax account is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Certificate of Incorporation to apply for the 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN); register concurrently for a GST/HST account (mandatory when taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a quarter or over four consecutive quarters), a payroll deductions (RP) account for employees, and a corporate income tax (RC) account; obtain the Letter of Confirmation from CRA for bank KYC and vendor onboarding.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Corporate registry abstract or certificate of existence
Directors' identification (passport or provincial ID) and SINs
RC1 request or online BRO submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA requires verification, provide notarized director/UBO declarations and a certified copy of the minute book; discrepancies are resolved via CRA Business Enquiries within 5-10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence, WCB Registration, and OHS Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal licensing authority (City of Calgary or City of Edmonton based on office location); Alberta Workers' Compensation Board (WCB); Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a General Business Licence from the local municipality if a physical office or storefront is established (home-based ICT businesses may require a home-based business permit); register with WCB within five days of hiring the first worker under the Workers' Compensation Act (NAICS 541512 classification unit); complete an OHS hazard assessment, first-aid and emergency response plan, and maintain a copy at the workplace under the OHS Code (Alta Reg 87/2009).
required_dossiers: Municipal general business licence application
Lease agreement and certificate of occupancy
WCB account registration form with industry classification
OHS workplace hazard assessment and first-aid plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal licence refusals can be appealed to the municipal licensing appeal committee; WCB assessment objections may be filed within 60 days under the Workers' Compensation Act; OHS compliance orders can be appealed to the Alberta OHS Appeals Office within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and AML/KYC Completion
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chartered banks and credit unions (e.g., RBC, TD, BMO, Scotiabank, ATB) subject to the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the corporate onboarding package to the commercial banking team; the bank completes KYC/AML verification of the entity, directors, officers, and every individual with significant control per the ABCA register (s. 114.5-114.7); execute a banking resolution specifying authorized signatories for Wise B2B, Payoneer, and SWIFT wire rails; complete the AML risk questionnaire (low-risk standard classification expected for ISIC 6202 non-financial services).
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and registry abstract
CRA BN confirmation letter
Register of directors and individuals with significant control (ISC)
Passports and proof of address of authorized signatories
Banking resolution of the board
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If KYC documentation is rejected or queried, supplement UBO source-of-funds evidence and updated government-issued IDs; request escalation to the commercial onboarding team; a second bank can be engaged without prejudice to the corporate registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no sectoral industrial licensing board regulates ISIC 6202 computer programming services in Alberta; a municipal general business licence and Alberta OHS registration apply only where a physical office is established
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal General Business Licence (City of Calgary / City of Edmonton) — required solely for physical premises; no provincial operating or manufacturing permit is required for a software development-only offshore delivery center

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based ICT consultancy services are not listed under the Environmental Assessment (Mandatory and Exempt Activities) Regulation, Alta Reg 111/1993; no EIA registration or full report required for the offshore development center activity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater or VOC emission thresholds apply to software engineering services; end-of-life IT hardware must not be landfilled and must be handled under the Electronics Recycling Regulation (Alta Reg 76/2004), with any waste transportation to an approved facility under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the municipal fire department under the Alberta Fire Code (Alta Reg 31/2003); building occupancy and structural load verification in accordance with the Alberta Building Code (Alta Reg 191/2006) for the leased office; OHS workplace compliance requiring a hazard assessment, emergency response plan, and first-aid supplies under the Occupational Health and Safety Code (Alta Reg 87/2009); WCB account in good standing prior to first employee hire.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC). Official portal: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; one-stop registration via CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/business-number.html. Alberta corporate income tax is administered federally by the CRA under the Alberta Tax Collection Agreement through the Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (ATRA); Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax, so no separate provincial indirect-tax registration exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Procedure for the foreign parent to establish the Alberta ODC (CA_CORP) and obtain the statutory tax identity: (1) Incorporate under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) or federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act followed by Alberta extra-provincial registration; obtain the corporate registry number. (2) Apply through the CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) portal for the 9-digit Business Number (BN) and simultaneously open program accounts RC (corporate income tax), RT (GST/HST), and RP (payroll if employees are hired). (3) Provide the CRA with the articles of incorporation, registered office address in Alberta, full names and residential addresses of directors (non-resident directors are permitted), and the foreign ultimate parent's identification; no minimum capital is required and unrestricted non-resident ownership is allowed. (4) Alberta corporate income tax registration is automatic through the federal T2 return; separate ATRA registration is not required. (5) The foreign parent itself does not require a Canadian BN unless it separately carries on business in Canada, makes taxable supplies in Canada, or has Canadian-source income subject to Part XIII withholding; dividend payments to the parent are reported on NR4 returns and treaty relief is applied through CRA Form NR301. (6) GST/HST registration is mandatory when annual worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000; a small supplier may voluntarily register earlier to claim input tax credits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. An Alberta business corporation (Inc./Corp.) is a separate Part I taxpayer under the Income Tax Act: federal general rate 15% plus Alberta general rate 8% = 23% combined. Territorial_Scope: a resident corporation (incorporated in Canada under ITA s. 250(1)(a)) is taxed on worldwide income; a non-resident corporation is taxed only on Canadian-source business income attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment, Canadian-source capital gains, and Part XIII withholdings. No pass-through eligibility exists for corporations, Canada has no tax-exempt zones, and the Alberta ODC is not eligible for any special economic-zone exemption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box election. Hybrid mismatch and reverse-hybrid rules (ITA ss. 12.3, 18.2, 18.3, 20.2) apply automatically, and no domestic election can disapply them. GST/HST election available: the ETA s. 156(2) close-connection election permits nil-consideration treatment for taxable supplies between closely related registrants, which may simplify intercompany shared-service billing while preserving full input tax credit recovery. For Part XIII withholding on dividends paid to the foreign parent, the parent files CRA Form NR301 for treaty-based rate reduction; this is an annual administrative application, not an entity-classification election.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification_note: The string above integrates the schema label and the Canadian legal effect.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms_note: The string above integrates the schema label and the Canadian legal effect.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST). Alberta is a non-participating province applying only the federal 5% GST; Alberta does not levy a provincial sales tax (PST) and is not an HST province.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000. The ODC ceases to be a small supplier when its annual worldwide taxable supplies, including supplies of associated persons, exceed CAD 30,000 (Excise Tax Act s. 240); registration is mandatory and the application must be filed within 30 days after the small-supplier status ceases. Voluntary registration is available to claim input tax credits before the threshold is crossed.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), or digital stamping regime. E-invoicing is voluntary under the Pan-Canadian Peppol framework, with a phased mandate for suppliers to the Government of Canada to transmit e-invoices through the federal e-invoice portal. Invoices must be issued and records retained for six years under ETA s. 286; GST/HST returns are filed electronically via CRA GST/HST NETFILE, and corporations with annual gross revenues exceeding CAD 1,000,000 must file the T2 corporate return and related schedules electronically. No API-based government pre-clearance of individual invoices is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The ODC's software engineering, development, maintenance, and outsourcing services qualify for the 0% GST rate as services supplied to a non-resident under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7, provided: (i) the foreign client is not a GST/HST registrant; (ii) the services are not in respect of real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada; and (iii) no part of the service is rendered to an individual who is present in Canada. Exported tangible deliverables qualify under Schedule VI, Part V, ss. 1 and 2 if exported as of the time of payment or delivered outside Canada. If the foreign client is a GST/HST registrant, the supply is generally taxable at 5% unless the service is delivered for use entirely outside Canada; the ODC should obtain and keep evidence of the client's non-resident status, including a certificate of residence, incorporation documents, and confirmation of no Canadian establishment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) - required only for tangible hardware or equipment physically exported; not filed for purely electronic software development services
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the carrier evidencing shipment of any exported goods delivered with the service
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, or bank statement of the ODC evidencing receipt of export consideration in CAD or convertible foreign currency
Executed master services agreement, purchase order, and zero-rated commercial invoices identifying the non-resident client and stating the 0% GST treatment under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7

Corporate records proving the client's non-resident status, such as certificate of incorporation, registered office address, tax residence certificate, and declaration that the client is not a GST/HST registrant
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada does not impose a statutory FX repatriation deadline; however, CRA audit scrutiny will test whether intercompany export receivables are collected on arm's length terms under ITA s. 247, and a stale receivable may give rise to transfer pricing adjustments, imputed interest, or shareholder-benefit treatment. If export zero-rating is denied for inadequate documentation, the CRA reassesses 5% GST on the full consideration plus compounded quarterly interest; the normal reassessment window is 4 years, extended to 10 years for misrepresentation or negligence, and unlimited for fraud. Civil penalties include ETA s. 280 failure-to-file penalties, ETA s. 285 false-statement penalties of CAD 250 or 25% of net tax, ETA s. 273 wilful-evasion penalties of 50% of tax sought to be evaded, ITA s. 163(2) gross-negligence penalties of 50% of understated income tax, and ITA s. 247(3) transfer-pricing penalties of 10% of the net adjustment (minimum CAD 5,000). Criminal prosecution is possible under ETA s. 327 and ITA s. 239; the ODC must retain all export documentation for at least six years.

stage_3.extra_fields_note: The two 'note' keys inside national_tax_registration_infrastructure were added by the assistant to clarify schema-label handling and are harmless; they can be removed if strict validation is required.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full capital account convertibility under IMF Article VIII status with no restrictions on capital movements or profit remittances from Canadian subsidiaries to foreign parents. Current account transactions, including dividends, management fees, and service payments, are fully convertible without prior approval or convertibility hurdles, subject only to standard tax filings, beneficial ownership reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), and FINTRAC compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from services (software engineering and maintenance) are classified as current account items. No statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratios to CAD apply. Funds may be retained in foreign currency accounts or repatriated freely, provided all foreign exchange transactions comply with FINTRAC reporting thresholds (e.g., CAD 10,000 cash transactions) and anti-money laundering obligations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for digital EMIs through platforms such as Wise Business and Payoneer for cross-border transfers. Legal constraints require registration with FINTRAC as a Money Services Business, full KYC/AML adherence under the PCMLTFA, and integration of offshore wallets with Canadian compliance controls to mitigate sanctions and regulatory risks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote KYC and corporate account opening is fully permitted under the Canada Business Corporations Act and Alberta Corporate Registry requirements. Directors and officers may complete verification remotely via video conferencing or digital document submission; physical presence is not mandated unless the institution classifies the account as high-risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or shell company structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ultimate beneficial owner declarations, Alberta Corporate Registry extracts, and independent third-party verification reports
Detailed transaction histories, client onboarding questionnaires, and comprehensive due diligence reports

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are processed via SWIFT MT103 wires using purpose code 'C' (Capital). Verification requires board resolutions, ownership percentages, proof of funds origin, and full client identification data as mandated by FINTRAC guidelines.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements utilize SWIFT MT103 for wire transfers and issuance of commercial letters of credit (LCs) through correspondent banks. Software service payments to vendors or affiliates are routed with supporting invoices and contracts; all outflows exceeding FINTRAC thresholds are reported.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency swaps for multi-currency liquidity management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Alberta Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the anniversary date of incorporation, amalgamation, or continuation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of CAD 100; prolonged default of two or more consecutive annual returns may result in administrative strike-off and dissolution by the Registrar after notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the taxation year-end; for a December 31 year-end, the filing deadline is June 30 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month late, up to 12 months; CRA may also assess a repeated failure penalty and charge arrears interest.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit for this private exempt Alberta business corporation engaged in offshore software development services. An audit may be statutorily required only if the corporation becomes a reporting issuer or a regulated entity, or if shareholders representing at least 5% of issued voting shares request an audit under the Alberta Business Corporations Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for Canadian reporting issuers; private corporations may select Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under the CPA Canada Handbook or voluntary IFRS adoption.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not require a separate annual UBO confirmation declaration. The corporation must maintain an internal register of individuals with significant control, updated within 15 days of any share transfer or change in control. The Alberta Annual Return confirms the registered office and current director information, providing an annual administrative verification point for the register.
